issues.description: Method name mismatch: the template declares StockIngredient.retrieveQuantity() but other artifacts expect StockIngredient.getQuantity(). Specifically, the template StockIngredient class provides retrieveQuantity(), while the template Stock class calls getQuantity() (causing a compilation error). The solution repository uses getQuantity(), and the problem statement requires adding getters for private fields, so the template's retrieveQuantity() name conflicts with the rest of the code and blocks successful compilation.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method StockIngredient.retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity(), matching the method calls in Stock and the solution. Alternatively, add a public getQuantity() method that delegates to retrieveQuantity(). Ensure the getter naming follows the convention used elsewhere so the template compiles and fulfills the problem statement requirement to provide getters for all private fields.

issues.description: The concept is the getter for the StockIngredient.quantity field. The problem statement instructs students to "add getters for all the private fields" (problem_statement.md calls for standard getters). In the template implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) the method is named retrieveQuantity(), whereas the rest of the template code (e.g., src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java and Main.java) and the provided solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) use getQuantity(). This naming mismatch prevents students from mapping the requirement to the template, will cause compilation errors (Stock calls getQuantity()), and increases cognitive load because students must deduce which getter to use or rename methods to make the code compile.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() so the getter name matches the standard convention and the usages in Stock.java and Main.java. Alternatively, add a getQuantity() method in the template that delegates to retrieveQuantity(), but the preferred fix is to use getQuantity() directly to align with the solution and the problem statement's expectation.
